report.verdict: An emergency department nurse manager whose profile shows how her team improved patient flow and nurse retention.
write_up: You lead an emergency department at a Level II trauma center, and a recruiter can see what changed under your leadership! Your headline names the job, and your About gets straight to the patient flow work.

The Saguaro Valley manager job is the model: it connects front-door triage and an overflow plan to fewer patients leaving without being seen. It also gives the turnover and labor budget results, so a recruiter doesn't have to guess what you manage.

Your profile isn't likely to be the thing standing between you and a message. Whether someone reaches out also depends on the roles available and your stated preference that you're not looking. If you later pursue a director role, you could add any work you've done planning resources beyond the ED.

cards.where: Saguaro Valley Medical Center, Nurse Manager description
cards.line: Cut left-without-being-seen from 5.1% to 2.3% in two years with front-door triage and a new overflow plan.
cards.cannot_tell: This is the line to keep as a model. It names the changes your team made and the patient flow measure that moved.

cards.where: Saguaro Valley Medical Center, Nurse Manager description
cards.line: Own a $14.5M labor budget; finished the last two fiscal years within 1% of plan.
cards.cannot_tell: The budget result is strong. For a director role, a recruiter may also look for resource planning beyond the ED, if that's work you've done.

cards.question: If you've planned staffing or resources beyond the ED, what did you do?

fit.why: Your headline and current job both describe leading an emergency department, with earlier bedside and charge nurse work.
fit.level: manager, your current Nurse Manager, Emergency Department title
fit.note: 'Emergency Department Nurse Manager' is in your headline. 'Nurse Staffing' and 'Trauma Care' are in your top skills, and 'split-flow' is in your About. Patient safety and quality improvement are other terms someone hiring for this work might use, if they describe your responsibilities.
